Dashboard user guide: presenting the dual-interface testbed

For a student who has never used the dashboard and has to demonstrate the project to an evaluation panel. Every screenshot here was taken from the real dashboard (http://localhost:8080) while its own buttons were pressed in the order of Part B, on run PANEL_20261124-182143 (simulated chamber, seed 42). That run's checker verdict was PASS. The red numbered circles are added afterwards (docs/user_guide/annotate.py) and are referred to as ① ② … below.

What the project is, in one sentence: one simulated process chamber whose state lives in one equipment core and is served at the same time over SECS/GEM (HSMS, port 5000) and OPC UA (port 4840). Every command from any side goes through one arbiter, and a checker proves from the logs whether both sides saw the same truth. This is a GEM-inspired testbed on one laptop (loopback). It is not GEM-compliant and has not been validated in a fab.

Before the panel (5 minutes earlier):

cd D:\semi-dual-testbed
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m harness.web_view --port 8080

Open http://localhost:8080 in the browser and make the window wide (1800 px or full screen). The page needs no internet. Keep a second terminal ready for the fallback in Part C.

Part A: Dashboard tour

A.1 Header, control panel and architecture

#ElementWhat it showsWhere the data comes fromColours
①LIVE / REPLAY badgeWhether the page follows a running system (LIVE) or plays back a finished run (REPLAY ×speed).The dashboard's own mode.Violet = informational.
②run badgeFolder name of the run being shown, runs/<run id>/. Panel runs are called PANEL_<date>-<time>.Newest run folder.—
③control badgeThe GEM control state: ONLINE_REMOTE, ONLINE_LOCAL or EQUIPMENT_OFFLINE.Core audit log (core_audit.jsonl).Blue = REMOTE (host in charge), green = LOCAL (operator in charge), amber = OFFLINE.
④processing badgeIDLE or EXECUTING (heater on).Core audit log.Amber = EXECUTING.
⑤authority badgeWho may currently command the tool: GEM_HOST, OPERATOR or UA_CLIENT. It follows from the control state and the maintenance lease.Core audit log.Violet.
⑥GEM link badgeWhether the HSMS connection between equipment and GEM host is up (COMMUNICATING) or down (NOT_COMMUNICATING).Equipment side of the GEM door.Green = up, red = down (it flashes when the link drops).
⑦TabsLive (this page), Inside (policy, model browser, race demo, A.4), Results (committed scenario results).—Blue = selected tab.
⑧Start system / Stop systemStart launches the equipment, a listening GEM host and a listening OPC UA client, like the scripted demo. Stop shuts them all down, runs the checker on the run, and verifies that ports 5000/4840/5100/5101 were released. The text next to the buttons shows RUNNING/STOPPED.harness/control_panel.py.Buttons are greyed out when they cannot be used.
⑨tshark line / verdict lineLive packet counts on ports 5000 and 4840 from tshark (Wireshark's command-line capture), shown if tshark is installed. After Stop system this line shows the checker verdict of the panel run.tshark on the loopback adapter.PASS green, FAIL red.
⑩GEM host rowGEM START / GEM STOP send a real S2F41 remote command over HSMS. Set limit (GEM) sends S2F15 (equipment-constant write). Kill GEM host kills the host process (simulated crash). Reconnect GEM host starts it again.Requests go through the listening GEM host's command port (5101), so they are real SECS-II messages.—
⑪OPC UA client rowUA Start / UA Stop call the OPC UA methods Start() / Stop(). Set limit (UA) calls SetTempHighLimit(value). Both START at once fires a GEM START and a UA Start released by one barrier (the same mechanism as scenario S3).Each press runs the real clients.ua_client program (an OPC UA Call on port 4840).—
⑫Operator rowREMOTE / LOCAL / OFFLINE change the control state. Lease UA / Lease off grant or revoke the maintenance lease (only possible in OFFLINE).Equipment operator console socket (port 5100).—
⑬Result boxThe real reply to the last button: HCACK (S2F42), EAC (S2F16), OPC UA StatusCode or console reply, plus the core's reason and the round-trip time.The reply the protocol returned.Green border = accepted, red border = rejected.
⑭ArchitectureOne core with the arbiter, two "doors" (secsgem and asyncua) and their clients. Moving dots are messages.Core audit log and the clients' receive logs.Green dot = accepted command or delivered event, red dot = rejected command, amber dot = alarm. A dashed red link with "✕ dropped_no_link" means the door had an event but no connected host to send it to.

Every button goes through an entry point that any outside client would use. The dashboard never calls the core directly, so the arbiter treats a button press exactly like a real host or client.

A.2 What each side sees, temperature, arbiter decisions, event timeline

#ElementWhat it showsWhere the data comes fromColours
⑮What each side seesThree columns of the same quantities: GEM host sees | Core (truth) | OPC UA client sees. Rows: temperature, control state, processing state, authority, TempHighLimit, alarm 5001, last event seq, last rejection, events received, GEM link.Left: what the GEM host logged as received (gem_host.jsonl). Middle: the core audit log. Right: what the OPC UA client logged (ua_client.jsonl).The core column is cyan. A red cell means that side currently disagrees with the core.
⑯Temperature rowIn this screenshot the GEM column is red: the GEM host had been killed, so its last temperature is stale while the core and OPC UA keep updating. That is exactly what the red highlight is for.
⑰GEM link rowThe link state as each side last reported it. A killed host cannot report that it died, so its own column still says COMMUNICATING (red, stale) while the core says NOT_COMMUNICATING.
⑱Core temperatureTemperature over the last 120 s, the TempHighLimit (dashed red line) and periods where alarm 5001 was active (amber band).Core audit samples.Cyan line = temperature, dashed red = limit, amber = alarm active.
⑲Arbiter decisionsEvery command that reached the arbiter, newest first: time, audit seq, origin (GEM_HOST / UA_CLIENT / OPERATOR), action, ACCEPTED/REJECTED and the reason.Core audit log (command_ok, command_rejected, ec_write, ec_rejected).Rejected rows have a red background.
⑳Event timelineOne row per event the core emitted (sequence number, core time, event name), and for each client whether and how fast it received it.Core audit log + both receive logs + both send-side logs (gem_adapter_send.jsonl, ua_adapter_send.jsonl).✓ + latency = received. … = not yet received. Red ✕ dropped_no_link = the door recorded that it could not send because no host was connected. Amber = alarm events.
㉑Dropped rowsEvents the GEM door could not deliver while the GEM host was down. There is no spooling, so they are lost, but every loss has a recorded cause (invariant I6).

A.3 On the wire and live invariants

#ElementWhat it showsWhere the data comes fromColours
㉒SECS-II on port 5000Every HSMS message, newest first, in SML (the standard text form of SECS-II). Examples: S6F11 W event report (equipment → host) with its full body, S2F41 W remote command, S2F42 reply, S5F1 alarm report, and HSMS control messages such as Select.req and Linktest. In an S6F11 the first number is DATAID (set to the event's sequence number), followed by the CEID and the report values.secsgem's own communication log inside the equipment (gem_wire.jsonl).Green header = equipment → host, cyan header = host → equipment.
㉓OPC UA on port 4840The OPC UA service calls and notifications: sessions, CreateSubscription, CreateMonitoredItems, Call (Start/Stop/SetTempHighLimit), and every Publish: DataChangeNotification and Publish: EventNotification.The OPC UA clients' own logs (ua_wire_*.jsonl). This is the client-API level, not decoded packets. Decoded packets are in results/demo_capture.pcapng (Wireshark).Green header = client → server, cyan header = server → client. Status Good green, Bad… red.
㉔Live invariantsThe checker (harness/checker.py) run on the logs so far, per invariant and per side. I1 completeness, I2 order, I3 value agreement, I4 state convergence within 500 ms, I5 single winner in conflicts, I6 every loss explained.The same checker code that judges the scenarios.PASS green, FAIL red, N/A grey (for example I5 when no conflict round has happened yet).
㉕CountersEvents received, missing, duplicates, out-of-order, value mismatches, losses with a recorded cause, unexplained losses, for GEM and UA.Checker.Red if a "bad" counter is above 0. "Losses with a recorded cause" may be above 0 and is still fine.
㉖Latency linep50/p95/max event latency per side (client receive time − core time).Checker.The OPC UA number includes the client's 50 ms publishing interval, so it is not a protocol speed comparison.
㉗Overall verdictPASS only if every applicable invariant passes.Checker.

A.4 Inside tab: policy, model browser, race demo

#ElementWhat it shows
㉘Inside tabClick it to see the three panels below.
㉙Control-authority policyWho may START / STOP / write the limit, for each control state. The table is generated by calling the arbiter's own decide() function, not copied from the documents. The row matching the current state is highlighted (blue frame). Green = allowed, red = rejected with the reason, amber = partly allowed (the operator's STOP-only safety override in REMOTE).
㉚Browse the server nowPerforms a real OPC UA browse of opc.tcp://127.0.0.1:4840 (system must be running) and prints the address space: object and variable types, live values, engineering units, ranges and methods.
㉛GEM link tags⟷ GEM SVID 1 (F4) etc.: every GEM-mapped OPC UA variable carries its GEM ID, kind and format (properties GemId/GemKind/GemFormat), so a UA client can navigate from a UA node to the GEM ID. This is the GEM-derived draft information model (N2).
㉜Race demo200 pairs of concurrent START commands, run twice. The unsafe variant (exists only in harness/race_demo.py) checks, releases the lock, waits 1 ms and then applies: both commands win almost every time. The real EquipmentCore decides and applies under one lock: never two winners. Both use the same arbiter in EQUIPMENT_OFFLINE + UA lease, where both contenders are allowed, so only atomicity makes the difference. It runs in-process and does not touch the running system.

A.5 Results tab

The Results tab lists the committed scenario summaries (results/summary.md, S1_summary.md … S6_summary.md, checker_self_test.md, capture_summary.md). Known issue: in the current dashboard version the Results tab stays on "loading…" (see Part C, "Results tab shows loading…"). Until that is fixed, open results/summary.md directly in the editor or on GitHub.

A.6 Known harmless effects (say this if the panel asks about a red cell)

  • Brief red cells in the OPC UA column. The OPC UA client receives data changes in batches every 50 ms (its publishing interval), while the core column updates immediately. Right after a change the UA cell can be red for up to about 0.1 s. Invariant I4 allows 500 ms and the measured maximum is far below that.
  • Red GEM cells after the GEM host is killed, and after Stop system. A dead or stopped host cannot log anything more, so its column keeps the last values it received (for example GEM link = COMMUNICATING) while the core moved on. Red here means "this side is stale". That is what the view is meant to show, not a bug.
  • Empty or N/A invariants in the first 2 seconds. The live checker only judges events older than 2 s, because younger ones may still be in flight. Right after Start system the invariants table is empty or N/A. I5 stays N/A until a Both START at once conflict has happened.
  • UA losses at start-up. The OPC UA door can log 1–2 dropped_no_link events in the first second, before the client has subscribed. They have a recorded cause and are counted by I6, not as failures.
  • The GEM I2 gaps 1 line after a reconnect. The events missed while the host was down are a gap in its sequence. Gaps are judged by I1/I6 (every one explained), so I2 still passes.

Part B: Demo script

About 6–8 minutes. Read the "What to say" column almost word for word. It is accurate and makes no claims about GEM compliance or protocol speed. Screenshots of each step follow the table.

StepClickWhat appearsWhat to say to the panel
1▶ Start systemAfter ~5 s: RUNNING, GEM link COMMUNICATING, the three columns fill, the tshark packet counts start rising, temperature ~25 °C."One simulated chamber, one core. The same state is now served by a SECS/GEM interface on port 5000 and an OPC UA server on port 4840, and a real GEM host and a real OPC UA client are both connected."
2REMOTEReply OK seq=…. control = ONLINE_REMOTE, authority = GEM_HOST, highlighted policy row changes."In ONLINE_REMOTE the GEM host holds command authority. The arbiter derives authority from the control state, and that rule is written down and tested."
3GEM STARTReply HCACK 0. processing = EXECUTING on all three columns; temperature starts rising."That was a real S2F41 remote command over HSMS. HCACK 0 means accepted, and the OPC UA client sees the same state change."
4(wait ~15 s)Temperature crosses the 40 °C limit. Alarm 5001 = SET in all three columns, amber band on the chart, ALID 5001 SET in the timeline with ✓ for both sides."The over-temperature alarm arrives as S5F1 on the GEM side and as an alarm event on OPC UA. Both carry the same sequence number, which the checker uses to join the two sides."
4a(scroll to "On the wire")Point at an S6F11 W on the left and the Publish: EventNotification on the right with the same number: in the S6F11 the first <U1 …> (DATAID) and the <U4 …> value are the seq; on OPC UA it is "EventSeq": … (figure B14)."Here is proof that both protocols are real: the same event, sequence number 45, once as a SECS-II S6F11 report and once as an OPC UA EventNotification."
5UA StartReply StatusCode BadUserAccessDenied · reason: authority held by GEM_HOST. A red row in Arbiter decisions; "Last rejection" updates on all three columns."The OPC UA client may not command the tool while the GEM host has authority. It gets a standard OPC UA status code, and the GEM host is told about the rejected attempt as well, through CEID 1005."
6GEM STOPHCACK 0, processing = IDLE, the temperature falls, and the alarm clears below 39 °C (hysteresis)."Stopping cools the chamber. The alarm clears with 1 °C hysteresis, on both sides again."
7⚡ Both START at onceGEM HCACK 0 | UA BadUserAccessDenied [conflict round … judged by I5]. Two decisions with consecutive seqs in the feed."Both commands were released at the same instant. Decide-and-apply happens atomically under one lock, so exactly one can win, and the policy says it must be the GEM host. Scenario S3 does this 50 times, and the unit test 500 times."
8(GEM STOP to return to IDLE), then LOCALOK, control = ONLINE_LOCAL, authority = OPERATOR."Now the operator takes the tool into LOCAL."
9GEM STARTHCACK 2 · reason: equipment in LOCAL, a red row in the feed."HCACK 2 means 'cannot perform now'. The host is refused because the operator has authority, and the reason is recorded in the audit log."
10REMOTEAuthority back to GEM_HOST."Back to remote control."
11Kill GEM hostGEM link = NOT_COMMUNICATING (red, flashing). The GEM link on the diagram turns dashed red."I have just simulated a host crash. The OPC UA side is unaffected: a failure of one interface does not stop the core or the other interface."
12(wait 10 s)Timeline: every new event shows ✕ dropped_no_link for GEM and ✓ for UA. The GEM column turns red (stale)."Neither secsgem nor OPC UA spools events. Events the GEM side misses are lost, but the GEM door logs every one it could not send, so each loss has a recorded cause. That is invariant I6. GEM spooling is one of the semantic gaps we document."
13Reconnect GEM hostGEM host connected, reports defined again. GEM link COMMUNICATING, ✓ marks for GEM again."The host reconnects, defines its reports again and receives new events. The old ones are not replayed."
14(optional) Inside tab → Browse the server now, then Run race demoModel tree with GEM IDs (SVID 1–5, ECID 201). Race result: unsafe 200/200 double winners, real 0/200."This is a live browse of our draft information model: every OPC UA variable carries its GEM ID. The race demo shows why the core must decide and apply atomically: with an artificial gap between check and apply, both commands win; in the real core never."
15Live tab → ■ Stop systemAfter ~10 s: STOPPED, last panel run: checker PASS · ports released: True."Stopping runs the same consistency checker as our scenarios on everything that just happened: completeness, order, value agreement, convergence within 500 ms, a single winner, and an explanation for every lost event."

Run used for the screenshots: PANEL_20261124-182143. Replies observed (from docs/user_guide/raw/run_log.txt):

remote -> Operator console: remote | reply: OK seq=29 (27 ms)
gem_start -> GEM host: S2F41 START (via the GEM host's command port) | reply: HCACK 0 (29 ms)
ua_start -> UA client: Call Start() (ua_client one-shot) | reply: StatusCode BadUserAccessDenied · reason: authority held by GEM_HOST (582 ms)
gem_stop -> GEM host: S2F41 STOP | reply: HCACK 0 (7 ms)
both_start -> GEM S2F41 START + UA Call Start released by one barrier (like S3) | reply: GEM HCACK 0 | UA BadUserAccessDenied [conflict round (authority GEM_HOST) - judged by I5] · reason: authority held by GEM_HOST (28 ms)
gem_stop -> GEM host: S2F41 STOP | reply: HCACK 0 (46 ms)
local -> Operator console: local | reply: OK seq=153 (4 ms)
gem_start -> GEM host: S2F41 START (via the GEM host's command port) | reply: HCACK 2 · reason: equipment in LOCAL (42 ms)
remote -> Operator console: remote | reply: OK seq=174 (15 ms)
kill_gem -> Kill the GEM host process (simulated crash) | reply: GEM host process killed (HSMS link will drop) (155 ms)
reconnect_gem -> Start the GEM host again | reply: GEM host connected, reports defined again (444 ms)

Part C: If something goes wrong

ProblemWhat you seeWhat to do
Port busyStart system reports an error mentioning a port, or nothing starts. Ports 5000 (HSMS), 4840 (OPC UA), 5100 (console), 5101 (GEM host relay) must be free. Port 8080 is the dashboard itself.Find the owner: Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 5000,4840,5100,5101 -State Listen | Select LocalPort,OwningProcess. If it is a leftover of this project (python.exe from D:\semi-dual-testbed\.venv), stop it with taskkill /T /F /PID <pid>. Do not kill unrelated Python programs.
System won't startState stays STARTING, or goes back to STOPPED with an error.Read runs/<newest PANEL run>/equipment.out and equipment.log. Close the dashboard (Ctrl+C in its terminal), check the ports as above, start the dashboard again and press Start system again.
A button says "system not running"All command buttons are greyed out.Press Start system first and wait for RUNNING.
GEM commands time out after Kill GEM hostReply shows an error.Press Reconnect GEM host first.
Model browser shows an error"connection refused"The browse needs the running system (OPC UA server on 4840). Start the system first.
Results tab shows "loading…"Known issue in this dashboard version (a name clash in web_view.html).Open results/summary.md in the editor instead.
Live demo is not possible at all—Switch to the replay dashboard. It plays back a committed real run and needs no equipment and no free ports except 8081: .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m harness.web_view --replay runs/sample_S3 --speed 3 --loop --port 8081, then open http://localhost:8081. It shows the same panels (header says REPLAY), without the control panel.
Dashboard page is blank / "reconnecting…"The dashboard process ended.Restart it (below) and reload the page.

Run every command from D:\semi-dual-testbed.

Live dashboard with control panel.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m harness.web_view --port 8080Ctrl+C in its terminal (it stops a running system too)

Equipment only.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m equipment.main (type help at its console)quit at its console
GEM host.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m clients.gem_host --listen (or Reconnect GEM host)Ctrl+C (or Kill GEM host)

If a dashboard was started in the background (no terminal window), stop it by its port owner: Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 8080 -State Listen → taskkill /T /F /PID <OwningProcess>.

How these screenshots were made

docs/user_guide/raw/ holds the unannotated full-page captures and, next to each, the measured element positions (*.json). They were taken by a headless Microsoft Edge that pressed the dashboard's own buttons through the browser (no direct API calls). The only change made to the page during capture was hiding the fixed footer, so that it does not overlap the full-page image. raw/run_log.txt lists every reply. annotate.py draws the callouts (Pillow), and build_pdf.py produces USER_GUIDE.html and USER_GUIDE.pdf with the images embedded.
